You are a programming expert. 
You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 

Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/sched/debug.c`**
- Removed the declaration of the `struct mempolicy *pol;`.
- Eliminated the `task_lock(p);` and `task_unlock(p);` calls that were used to lock the task structure.
- Removed the logic that checked for the memory policy (`pol`) and the associated `mpol_get(pol);` and `mpol_put(pol);` calls.
- The function `sched_show_numa()` now directly accesses the task's NUMA statistics without needing to manage memory policy or task locking.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in `sched_show_numa()` reflect a simplification of the function by removing unnecessary locking and memory policy management. This change is based on the fact that the format of the output has changed, making the previous handling of memory policies redundant. The removal of these elements enhances performance and reduces complexity, as the function no longer needs to manage the state of the task or its memory policy when displaying NUMA statistics. This patch addresses a specific bug related to NUMA balancing stats in the `/proc/pid/sched` interface, as indicated by the fix reference.

Here is the commit message:
sched/debug: Remove mpol_get/put and task_lock/unlock from
 sched_show_numa

The older format of /proc/pid/sched printed home node info which
required the mempolicy and task lock around mpol_get(). However
the format has changed since then and there is no need for
sched_show_numa() any more to have mempolicy argument,
asssociated mpol_get/put and task_lock/unlock. Remove them.

Fixes: 397f2378f1361 ("sched/numa: Fix numa balancing stats in /proc/pid/sched")
Signed-off-by: Bharata B Rao <bharata@amd.com>
Signed-off-by: Peter Zijlstra (Intel) <peterz@infradead.org>
Reviewed-by: Srikar Dronamraju <srikar@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
Acked-by: Mel Gorman <mgorman@suse.de>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220118050515.2973-1-bharata@amd.com

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the unnecessary locking and memory policy management in the `sched_show_numa()` function, which was no longer needed due to a change in the output format of the `/proc/pid/sched` interface. The presence of `mpol_get/put` and `task_lock/unlock` led to potential inefficiencies and complications in accessing NUMA statistics, which were not required for the current implementation.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void sched_show_numa(struct task_struct *p, struct seq_file *m)
 {
 #ifdef CONFIG_NUMA_BALANCING
-	struct mempolicy *pol;
-
 	if (p->mm)
 		P(mm->numa_scan_seq);
 
-	task_lock(p);
-	pol = p->mempolicy;
-	if (pol && !(pol->flags & MPOL_F_MORON))
-		pol = NULL;
-	mpol_get(pol);
-	task_unlock(p);
-
 	P(numa_pages_migrated);
 	P(numa_preferred_nid);
 	P(total_numa_faults);
 	SEQ_printf(m, "current_node=%d, numa_group_id=%d\n",
 			task_node(p), task_numa_group_id(p));
 	show_numa_stats(p, m);
-	mpol_put(pol);
 #endif
 }
